basic_info.title: Ontology-Based Map Data Quality Assurance
basic_info.venue: ESWC 2021 — The Semantic Web: 18th International Conference (Extended Semantic Web Conference), Virtual Event, June 6-10, 2021. Springer, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 12731, chapter 5

method.notes: Proposes an ontology-based (OWL/RDF) workflow for HD map data quality assurance with three stages: semantic enrichment of map data, logical violation (constraint) detection via reasoning, and on-the-fly (on-board, in-car) violation handling. Evaluation indicates the approach can successfully check map data quality and that violation handling is feasible on-the-fly in the vehicle.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: This work realizes the semantic-enrichment idea (thesis pillar P1b) SYMBOLICALLY through hand-authored OWL/RDF ontologies and logical reasoning rather than as learned, vectorized graph tokens consumed by a transformer. It targets map-data quality checking, not GPS map matching or path prediction, and contains no learned sequence model, no RL agent, and no label-free training on raw fleet trajectories.
gap_analysis.novelty_note: It is a genuinely distinct (symbolic/logical) approach to map semantics, leaving the learned-vectorized-encoder + latent-RL + label-free-trajectory hybrid entirely unaddressed.

relevance.bmw_relevance: HIGH — a BMW in-house semantic-map quality-assurance approach co-authored by the thesis interview lead Adel Ayara (with Glimm, Ulm University / BMW Car IT), directly informing the classical counterpart of the P1b semantic-enrichment pillar.
